hackathon.prizesDescription: Ship something great and compete for cash, credits, coworking, and scholarships.
hackathon.specialThanksDescription: The people and spaces that make this day possible.
hackathon.sponsorDescription: Support the hackathon and connect with Serbia's builder community. Tell us about your company and we'll get back to you with sponsorship options.
hackathon.messagePlaceholder: Tell us about your sponsorship interest or preferred tier.
hackathon.success: Thanks! We'll be in touch about sponsorship.
hackathon.requiredFields: Please fill in all required fields.
hackathon.invalidEmail: Please enter a valid email address.
hackathon.genericError: Something went wrong. Please try again.
hackathon.stackDescription: One card per tech partner, labeled by area of work. Click for technologies, use cases, and what you get.
hackathon.stackOverlapTitle: How they sit next to each other
hackathon.stackRecipesDescription: You can win with one tech partner used well. These combine two or three when you want a full story.
hackathon.stackHostNote: Build in Grok Bot — the host editor for this hackathon. Cursor works too.
hackathon.stackVoiceLaneNote: Wispr Flow is how you dictate into Grok Bot (or Cursor) — voice input for building, not TTS in the product.
hackathon.guideDescription: Rules, agenda, judging, guidelines, and optional idea sparks — build whatever you want.
hackathon.guideAgendaDescription: One full day in Belgrade. Times are local.
hackathon.guideTopicsEmpty: Challenge tracks are not published yet.
hackathon.peopleDescription: Ask early. Hosts help with anything. Mentors unblock the build and the story. Judges land as they are confirmed.
hackathon.mentorsDescription: Builders in the room. Come with a stuck demo or a GTM question — do not wait until the last hour.
hackathon.hostsDescription: Hosts running the Grok Bot Serbia Hackathon. Ask whatever you need — we are here to help.
hackathon.judgesDescription: The people who will watch the demos.
hackathon.judgesEmpty: Judges are not published yet. They will appear here as they lock.
hackathon.creditsHostClaimHint: Checked-in hackers get a unique $20 Cursor link and a unique $50 Cursor link — claim each once.
hackathon.creditsCursor20SetupTip: Redeem $20 Cursor credits → upgrade to Cursor Pro → log in to Grok Bot → you're all set
hackathon.creditsCursor50SetupTip: Redeem $50 Cursor credits on your Cursor account, then build in Grok Bot (or Cursor) for the day.
hackathon.creditsDaytonaRedeemTip: Create your Daytona account at app.daytona.io → go to Billing → paste your code → Redeem.
hackathon.creditsDaytonaRedeemProTip: Pro tip: paste Daytona’s LLMs text into your AI to quickly learn what the platform can do.
hackathon.creditsRenderRedeemTip: Go to dashboard.render.com/billing → scroll to Credit Balance → Enter promo code → Apply.
hackathon.creditsXaiRedeemTip: Open console.x.ai → Billing → Redeem promo code. Credits are ~$35 per Console team; 160 redemptions total, one per team. Valid Saturday 12 Sep 2026 (Belgrade time).
hackathon.creditsXaiRedeemProTip: Works for Voice / Chat / Imagine / Grok Build via a Console API key — does not work for Grok Bot.
hackathon.creditsNotCheckedIn: Check in at the event to claim
hackathon.submitPageDescription: Checked-in hackers submit one project per team for judging. Teams are 1–3 people. Names appear on the gallery; emails stay private. Resubmitting updates the same entry.
hackathon.submitNeedLogin: Sign in with Google to submit your project. You must also be checked in at the event.
hackathon.submitNeedCheckIn: You are registered, but not checked in yet.
hackathon.submitNeedCheckInHint: Find a host at the venue and check in on Luma before you can submit.
hackathon.submitNeedRegister: We could not find your Google email on the Luma guest list. Register for the hackathon first.
hackathon.submitStatusError: Could not verify your Luma status. Try again.
hackathon.submitTeammatesHint: Teams are 1–3 people — you plus up to 2 teammates. Use the Google email they sign in with. Names are shown publicly; emails stay private and keep the team to one project. Leave blank if you are solo.
hackathon.submitTeammateNeedsBoth: Each teammate needs both a display name and an email.
hackathon.submitTeammatePrefillBanner: You're on “{title}”, submitted by {name}. Updating this entry — one project per team.
hackathon.submitDescriptionPlaceholder: What you built, who it is for, and what judges should notice.
hackathon.submitGithubHint: Link to the project repo on GitHub (github.com/owner/repo).
hackathon.submitRecordingHint: Link to a 3–5 minute demo (YouTube, Loom, or similar — public or unlisted).
hackathon.submitSuccess: Project submitted. Judges will review your entry.
hackathon.submitUpdateSuccess: Project updated. Judges will see your latest entry.
hackathon.submitUpdateHint: Need to change something? Submit again — it updates your existing entry.
hackathon.submitPrefillBanner: We loaded your existing submission — edit anything and update.
hackathon.submitPrefillError: Could not load your existing submission. You can still fill the form.
hackathon.submitClosedBody: The submit form is no longer accepting new projects or updates.
hackathon.submitAdminClosed: Submissions are closed. Hackers cannot submit or update projects.
hackathon.submitCloseHint: Closing hides the form for everyone until you reopen it.
hackathon.submitGateError: Could not update the submissions gate.
hackathon.projectsPageDescription: Browse submitted projects, watch demos, open live apps, and vote for your favorites. Judges score privately 1–10; checked-in hackers can favorite up to three.
hackathon.projectsEmptyBody: Submissions will appear here once checked-in hackers submit via the Submit tab.
hackathon.projectsVoteHint: Sign in with Google and check in on Luma to favorite up to three projects.
hackathon.projectsNeedCheckIn: Check in at the event before favoriting projects.
hackathon.projectsNeedCheckInHint: Find a host at the venue and check in on Luma — then you can pick up to three favorites.
hackathon.projectsJudgeAlsoFavorite: Check in on Luma to also favorite community projects (up to 3).
hackathon.projectsJudgePanelDescription: Score each project 1–10. Your scores stay private until every judge marks scoring finished. Winners stay off the public gallery until an admin publishes.
hackathon.projectsJudgeAllRated: Every judge has scored every project
hackathon.projectsJudgeWaiting: Waiting for all judges to finish
hackathon.projectsJudgeFinishHint: This freezes your scores. You will not be able to change them afterward.
hackathon.projectsJudgeFinishedWaiting: Your scoring is final. Waiting for other judges ({finished} / {total}).
hackathon.projectsJudgeAllFinished: All judges have finished. Panel votes and winners are visible to judges only.
hackathon.projectsJudgeNeedsDecision: Needs admin decision — averages are tied for final placement.
hackathon.projectsJudgePrivacyNote: These votes are visible to judges and admins only. The public gallery stays unchanged until an admin publishes.
hackathon.projectsPublishHint: Show the judge top 3 on the public gallery.
hackathon.projectsJudgeSetTop3Hint: Pick the final 1st, 2nd, and 3rd to resolve the tie.
hackathon.projectsJudgeConfirmTop3Hint: Confirm or override the final top 3.
hackathon.projectsLeaderboardDescription: Top 3 projects by community favorites. Ties break by earlier submission, then title.
hackathon.projectsPreviewBanner: Preview mode — fixture projects for local UI demos (not live data).
